# Original Notes

The module author's raw notes, preserved unedited as the seed of this module. They set the reading brief: extract the ideas, and reframe the theory's stochasticity as inaccessibility-in-principle rather than destruction of information. Their development is [[vendor/postquantum-gravity/commentary/descent-instead-of-diffusion|descent instead of diffusion]].

Theory of gravity as essentially "stochastic" (that is, it violates the Unitarity Principle -- quantum information is destroyed)

This is very interesting, because it helps make the math of gravity tame and renormalizable.  It also does not need to deal with "ghosts" (negative probabilities)

I feel like this is a friend of my cosmodynamic project.  The key difference is that I don't want to think of gravity as "stochastic" -- that feels weird.  Check on the `causal-wall-spectral-theory` and the `sufficent-reason` modules to understand that "information is not destroyed" per se -- it was never accessible in principle!  There is a descent.

My model is dealing with gravity/space-time/matter as something like the "residue" or "cost" of that descent across a stack (mathematically).

The math & philosophy of this model could be a palatable framing for "postquantum gravity".
